RAMANAGARA, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 26.07.2021 passed in MVC.No.111/2016 on the file of the III Addl. District and SEsisons Judge &
MACT at Ramanagara Judge (for short 'the tribunal') on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.

III Addl. District and SEsisons Judge &
MACT at Ramanagara Judge
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
The claimant was riding a motorbike bearing No.KA-42-E- 1271 along with his wife Bhavya and his child proceeding towards Ramanagara from Bengaluru.

On 24.11.2015 motorcycle of the claimant was hit by a canter vehicle bearing No.KA-40-3632 from behind as the driver of the said vehicle NC: 2024:KHC:6500 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the vehicle of claimant.
Due to occurrence of the accident, the claimant sustained fracture of his lower end of his left radius and contusion injuries.
He took treatment with POP.
He stated that he spent an amount of Rs.20,000/- for the treatment and that he was working as a mason earning an amount of Rs.600/- per day.
However no documents are placed on record.

The tribunal after hearing the learned counsels of both the parties and on perusal of the materials placed before the court, awarded a compensation of an amount of Rs.58,000/- considering the objections raised by the respondent -insurance company.

4. The occurrence of the accident, the involvement of vehicle, the injuries sustained by claimants are not seriously disputed, but the learned counsel for the insurance company contends that the injury is very minor and simple in nature and as only POP is been applied without there being any surgical Chandrahshekar S vs Mumtaz Pasha on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82448423/
2 intervention.
The tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/- per month as no proof of income is placed.
However, the notional income prescribed by the NC: 2024:KHC:6500 Karnataka State Legal Services Authority chart for the year 2015 is Rs.9,000/-.
Hence, income of the claimant has to be taken as Rs.9,000/- per month as no proof of income is produced.
The doctor has been examined as PW-2 who has opined disability to an extent of 5.3% by producing disability certificate at Ex.P-9.
The tribunal has disbelieved the version of the doctor has not awarded any compensation on the ground of loss income due to disability.
To establish that there is disability and loss of future income except for the opinion of the doctor and disability certificate, no additional document is placed on record.
The Tribunal has not accepted the evidence of the doctor with regard to disability.

I am afraid the argument putforth by the learned counsel for the appellant cannot be accepted that there is disability of 5.3% on the basis of the opinion expressed by Doctor PW-2 for the reason even according to the claimant, he has been treated by applying POP and there is no surgical intervention.
Hence, the tribunal has rightly denied the loss of future income due to disability which is retained.
Towards pain and agony on account of fracture of lower end of left radius an amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded by the tribunal is retained.
6. Towards minimum medical expenses an amount of Rs.6,000/- is awarded and it is retained.
Towards loss of income during the laid up period for two months has been awarded.
The same has be enhanced as this court has enhanced income from Rs.6,000/- to Rs.9,000/- per month.

7. The claimant would be entitled for Rs.18,000/- as against Rs.12,000/- towards unhappiness and amenities an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded by the tribunal and this court awards an amount of Rs.25,000/-.

8. In view of the above discussion, the claimant is entitled for total compensation of amount of Rs.79,000/- as against Rs.58,000/- along with interest at 6% as mentioned in the table below:
NC: 2024:KHC:6500 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and Agony 30,000-00 Loss of Amenities 25,000-00 Loss of income during the laid up 18,000-00 period Medical Expenses 6,000-00  TOTAL 79,000-00
